name: Question 3
problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-10 & 16 & 8 \\ -6 & 20 & 6 \\ -12 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}14 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}1 & a & 0 \\ 2 & b & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ find the value of $2a-b.$
worked_solution:
From the diagonal matrix $D$, we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=14,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ ${\lambda }_{3}=8.$

So, the second column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector that corresponds to ${\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Computing $A-(-2)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-{\lambda }_{2}I & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & 16 & 8 \\ -6 & 20 & 6 \\ -12 & 4 & 10\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 16 & 8 \\ -6 & 22 & 6 \\ -12 & 4 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ that we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 16 & 8 & 0 \\ -6 & 22 & 6 & 0 \\ -12 & 4 & 12 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=-\frac{1}{8}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ -6 & 22 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & -40 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd ones). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=0.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$
Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the eigenvector 

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $2a-b=2\cdot 1-0=2.$
